new_evidence_added: Dome's own quiet test reproduced: BOU 1-min Z standard deviation over the whole UT day gives exactly 2.23 / 8.05 / 5.59 nT for 2016-03-09 / 2017-08-21 / 2024-04-08 (the dome's published values). 2026-08-12 = 7.62 nT -> FAILS the dome's < 5 nT rule. None of the 30 preceding days passes (5.49-15.21 nT, incl. Kp-1 days at 6.4 and 10.5) - the statistic is dominated by summer Sq at Boulder, so it cannot certify any summer day. Reported both ways (supports Option B formally; shows the rule acts as an unconditional escape clause for this event).
Quadratic-trend variant explains most of the rev2 Z-down obscuration fits (priority stations and ASC).
WIN-010 profile test result (dome-favourable vs our binary profile; not attributable to the eclipse).
E-PRED-B (dome: HAD signal > EBR signal) scored: unevaluable - no detectable signal at either station; ordering flips with metric, |diff| < 1.3 SD.
dome_favourable_findings_disclosed: 16:59 H drop coincides with dome global C1 (no longer used against the dome)
LER linear-trend Z fit -12.8 nT near -17 (power 0.60)
WIN-010 profile favours FSF over our binary profile on Z
Day fails the dome quiet test -> dome entitled to call the test void
kernel_of_truth: The dome is right that the day was not quiet by its own test, right that something happened at its global C1, and on the site-registered profile test its FSF ordering fits the Z residuals better than the crude profile we registered. None of that rescues the Tier-1 claim: the ECM-unique contact-phase signature is absent at every priority station at amplitudes the day could have shown, including the formula's own smaller ones.

anticipated_objections.objection: Dome defender: "You admit FSF beat your magnetic-latitude profile."
anticipated_objections.response: Yes, on Z, and we say so in the headline. The same eclipse day shows larger latitude-scaled Z structure two hours later with no eclipse, and FSF is tan(latitude), so any latitude-increasing external field favours it. Our profile lost; FSF physics did not win.

anticipated_objections.objection: Dome defender: "By my BOU rule the day was void, so any falsified label is illegitimate."
anticipated_objections.response: Agreed that the day failed the rule, which is why Option B exists. But the same rule fails every day of July-August 2026 including Kp-1 days, so it cannot distinguish quiet from disturbed in summer; the operator decides whether that makes it an escape clause (Option A).

anticipated_objections.objection: Our side: "Refuting our own upper band on a post-hoc rule is self-harm for symmetry's sake."
anticipated_objections.response: That is the point of the erratum symmetry obligation. The band was not computed for a sunset eclipse; its failure is ours (analyst_representation), not standard physics.

anticipated_objections.objection: Curmudgeon: "Quadratic trend is also post hoc; choosing it after seeing ASC is fitting the noise."
anticipated_objections.response: Both trend models are reported everywhere; no verdict depends on choosing quadratic. It is used only to explain the ASC/priority negative-Z fits and to show the BOU-formula power is variant-dependent.
